title: Intros, lead melody and bass figures on the Page session
summary: He explains kicking off tunes because he could play the melody, his many intro ideas and bass figures, and a Roy Rogers sideman who may have copied him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I'm going to play another tune. It'll be "Thirsty Mama Blues," which -- no, that was the one we just --
We just got finished with that one. Oh, the next one we're going to do is "Evil Man's Blues," where you do the vocal.
We can talk while that's playing.
We can talk while that's playing.
We can talk while it's playing and record at the same time. That's beautiful, huh?
Oh, you're letting her off the hook, though.
I'm giving her notice. That sure is cold. That sure is cold. You know he can't, but he wants to set her free.
That introduction is really typical of your work. Like it seems like a lot of these sessions you got to kick it off, you know.
Well, I was only the lead melody. See, I could play the melody.
I was the only one that could play the melody, so --
And then as soon as you're singing right here, you'd want to go into the chords.
I notice like your ideas are like -- there are so many different ideas.
Well, I had to think, you know.
I was thinking a lot there. All the time. It's a wonder I ain't blowed my top, to tell you the truth, because my mind was always going this way.
A lot of them of course are -- you take the ending and put it in the front, right?
Change the chords around a little bit.
Or go to a bass interpretation.
Whatever I though I had, I just played it to see if it would come out.
From what I heard it was worked all right. I was on every record session they had [for me.] I'm on all of them.
You know, it's interesting, some of those bass figures that you do, those kinds of things?
A lot of those figures I've never heard any other guitarist playing as many different variations on those figures in this period. But later on -- did you ever
The guys that backed up Roy Rogers.
The guitarist with them I think picked up on some of those because he used to use a lot of those figures.
He may have listened to you.
Because they were working in the '40s, when you were out here.
Of course a lot of people have the same ideas. They just float around.
They can hear something, you know, and they would like it --
Sure. It doesn't belong to anybody.
I think if somebody takes a whole solo and copies it, that's something else.
Yeah, then it belongs to somebody. They stole it from somebody.
I guess that's why I was getting so many sessions.
Because you were coming up with different ideas?
Yeah, different ideas all the time.
I was going to play some other recordings, but I was wondering if there was anything else you had to say about Hot Lips Page, or anything you remember about him.
Well, not too much now. I told you that much I knew right now.
Probably think about it (Unintelligible). after I get in bed, Start wailin' around a little bit.
